verdict.rationale: Morph's own docs claim high throughput for its specialized models: Fast Apply at 10,500 tok/s, Compact at 33,000 tok/s, and ~90ms classifiers. It also documents speed-relevant serving features: prefix caching on by default and dedicated reserved-capacity endpoints. However, nothing documents time-to-first-token or throughput for the general open-weight chat models, and all figures are vendor claims without independent benchmarks. Missing for 10: documented time-to-first-token figures, throughput/latency numbers for general chat generation (e.g. Kimi K3), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the speed claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve latency-sensitive workloads with fast time-to-first-token and high-throughput generation

citations.quote: Fast Apply merges just the changed lines at 10,500 tok/s, 98% accuracy.
Drop filler from chat history and code context at 33,000 tok/s.
Small text classifiers that label a turn in ~90ms
Prefix caching is on for every open source model. No configuration, no cache-write surcharge.
Reserve model capacity by choosing a model and plan. Morph provisions and operates it
